transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 mins
Recording: Fireflies auto-transcript
Shared links: https://redwood.app/decks/caspian-relevance, benchmark sheet: https://sheets.example.com/redwood-caspian-bench

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo showing embeddings + reranking endpoints, plus Console Optimize suggestions for batching/caching and an optional dedicated path for higher throughput. Customer cares about PII handling, SOC2, and on-prem future.

Topics:
- Current stack & pain: slow search, highly sensitive patient notes (PII), sporadic spikes in traffic
- Demo: embeddings endpoint, vector search + reranker (server-side rerank with hosted endpoint)
- Console: per-route latency/cost, rollout, and Optimize suggestions
- Security/compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logs, token retention

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on this -- and Samir who's our solutions engineer, hi Samir.
[00:00:09] Samir: hey all, hello.
[00:00:12] Maya: hi, thanks for making time. we squeezed in a few people here. I'm Maya, i own search at Caspian.
[00:00:18] Omar: Omar here, platform eng, i'll mostly be listening for infra bits.
[00:00:22] Priya: Priya, product, hi.
[00:00:25] Lena: Great. Goal for today is a short hosted API walkthrough: embeddings, vector retrieval, and an additional rerank step using Redwood's hosted reranker endpoint. We'll also show Console Optimize ideas that reduce token cost with caching and quantization recs. We'll keep it to ~45 minutes and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:40] Maya: perfect. quick note — our data is PHI adjacent, so we need encryption, KMS, and SOC2 evidence before we can pilot.
[00:00:46] Lena: understood, we'll link SOC 2 and network diagram after.
[00:00:50] Samir: ok jumping into the demo — i'm sharing my screen. apologies if the slides come through a bit fuzzy, network is meh.
[00:01:08] [00:01:08] Samir: (screen) here's the Console: model catalog at the top, hosted endpoints listed. We'll demo using rwd-embedding-512 for the vector index, then a small transformer reranker (rwd-rerank-tiny) for reordering top-K.
[00:01:25] Priya: quick q — can you run rerank server-side or do we have to fetch embeddings and do client side rerank?
[00:01:32] Samir: good q. You can do both. For faster ops we've got a hosted rerank endpoint where you send top-k candidates plus query context and we return reranked list. Client side is also possible if you want full control.
[00:01:45] [00:01:45] Samir: i'll show the flow: 1) call embeddings endpoint to get vectors for query, 2) do ANN search in your vector DB (we demo with in-memory here), 3) call Redwood rerank passing the candidate passages + query, 4) present top result.
[00:02:05] Omar: about latency — what should we expect for an end-to-end re-rank against top 10?
[00:02:09] Samir: on hosted, for a small reranker you should see ~60-120ms for the rerank call itself depending on payload size and model. End-to-end if you're doing ANN + network + rerank maybe 120-300ms. For hard SLOs we recommend Dedicated capacity or edge routing to region. Those numbers are ballpark, we'll run a small benchmark for your sample.
[00:02:28] Maya: and cost? reranking every query sounds expensive.
[00:02:31] Lena: yes cost vs quality is the classic tradeoff — Optimize can suggest a hybrid: run cheap lexical filter first, only rerank top N for ambiguous queries, and use prefix/KV cache for popular queries. That often cuts rerank invocations by 40-70%.
[00:02:45] [00:02:45] Samir: also our Console has telemetry that shows per-route tokens and per-token cost — we can set alerts if cost per query exceeds a threshold.
[00:02:55] Priya: Can we see an example with our type of content? health notes are long and have redacted fields.
[00:02:59] Samir: sure — i'm going to paste a sanitized sample into the demo notebook. note: this is a demo sandbox, not connected to your production.
[00:03:12] [00:03:12] Samir: (exec) embeddings call -> returns vector length 512, similarity search returns 15 candidates, feeding top 8 into reranker...
[00:03:30] [00:03:30] Samir: rerank call returns structured object: scores + normalized confidence. you'll see the top candidate has a stronger match and we also provide reasons (extractive highlights) if you enable structured output.
[00:03:45] Maya: those extractive highlights look useful — are those deterministic? sometimes the model picks different spans.
[00:03:50] Samir: they're model-derived; to increase determinism you can pin model versions or use lower-temperature rerankers. We also have eval hooks to run a prompt set and detect regressions over rollouts.
[00:04:05] [00:04:05] Lena: i want to surf to Console Optimize — this is where we suggest batching sizes per model, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles per workload. For embeddings-heavy workloads we often recommend increased batch sizes at low-latency mode if you have slight latency slack.
[00:04:21] Omar: batch sizes — but doesn't that increase tail latency? we have spikes during morning ingestion.
[00:04:25] Samir: it can increase per-request latency if you wait for batch fullness. Our runtime supports adaptive batching with latency SLOs: it will flush after X ms to meet SLO and still batch when possible. For spikes we recommend autoscaling Dedicated or tiered routing.
[00:04:41] Priya: what about data residency? we need EU-only storage for some customers.
[00:04:45] Lena: we can pin region for hosted endpoints; for stricter residency or air-gapped needs we offer Private (VPC or on-prem) which includes local KMS integrations. we'll attach the compliance pack for the pilot.
[00:04:58] [00:04:58] Maya: do you do token-level logging? our legal requires minimal retention.
[00:05:03] Samir: by default hosted has ephemeral request logs but you can disable payload logging; we provide audit logs that surface metadata but not full PII unless you enable it. For stronger controls, Dedicated or Private gives you full control over retention and KMS.
[00:05:18] [00:05:18] Samir: ok i'm switching to a small live rerank demo using a sample query: 'what are contraindications for drug X in elderly with renal impairment'
[00:05:25] [00:05:25] Samir: embeddings -> ann -> reranker (payload small) -> response in 95ms for rerank call, total end-to-end ~210ms in sandbox.
[00:05:38] Maya: that's promising. can you show the Console trace for that request?
[00:05:41] Samir: yep. (shares trace) you can see token counts, model latency, and the cost estimate. There's also a breakdown per-component.
[00:05:55] [00:05:55] Priya: On accuracy — do you have a way to tune reranker behavior? we sometimes want recall boosts over precision for clinical safety.
[00:06:03] Samir: yes you can supply a scoring bias, prefer recall by adjusting the cutoff or use model variants tuned for recall. Console Optimize recommends model + temperature + cutoff settings per your labeled eval set. We also support A/B rollouts so you can measure real user impact.
[00:06:20] [00:06:20] Omar: For pilot scale — 10k queries/day, 5M docs corpus — what's a sensible plan?
[00:06:26] Lena: for that size hosted is reasonable to start; we recommend caching hot queries and using a small reranker first. If throughput grows above ~50 qps sustained with rerank, we typically discuss Dedicated. I'll include sizing notes in the follow-up.
[00:06:40] Maya: ok good. security checklist — will you send the KMS integration docs and network diagram?
[00:06:45] Lena: yes.
[00:06:48] [00:06:48] Samir: switching to Console Optimize -> here's the 'suggested changes' card. For your workload it suggests: increase embedding batch from 4 -> 16, enable prefix cache with 24h TTL for commonly repeated queries, use 8-bit quantized model variant for embeddings to save tokens and speed up throughput.
[00:07:06] Priya: 8-bit quant — any quality regression risks?
[00:07:09] Samir: some, but for embeddings it's minimal. For rerankers we recommend validation against your eval set; Optimize gives an estimated quality delta. We'll run a small pre/post eval during the pilot.
[00:07:22] [00:07:22] Maya: do you integrate with our vector DB or do we need to host it?
[00:07:26] Samir: Redwood doesn't force a vector DB — you can keep your existing DB. We offer connectors for common stores and a managed index for quick start. For private deployments we can ship a connector for your internal store.
[00:07:39] [00:07:39] Priya: what's the onboarding timeline? from pilot to production?
[00:07:42] Lena: pilot 2-4 weeks, then production phased rollout over 4-8 weeks depending on compliance checks and traffic shaping.
[00:07:50] [00:07:50] Omar: about SSO and RBAC — we use Okta and have strict roles.
[00:07:54] Lena: we support SAML/SSO with SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC in Console at route/model level. We'll include our SSO integration guide.
[00:08:05] [00:08:05] Maya: any blockers we should be aware of from infra? network, firewall, egress?
[00:08:09] Samir: for hosted, you just need outbound to our API endpoints; for VPC/Private we do a handshake with your infra team to open secure tunnels and configure KMS. We'll send a sample network diagram.
[00:08:23] [00:08:23] Priya: who are your main competitors in this space — just to understand differences?
[00:08:27] Lena: broadly OpenAI/Anthropic for model access, Google Cloud for managed endpoints, and a few inference infra vendors. We differentiate on runtime optimizations, unified hosted/dedicated/private, and first-class observability for cost/latency.
[00:08:41] Maya: can we do an eval with our labeled pairs to quantify lift?
[00:08:45] Samir: absolutely — send us 2-3k labeled pairs and we'll run an eval and a recommended config.
[00:08:54] [00:08:54] Lena: ok wrapping into a quick pilot plan: 1) Caspian provides 10k sample queries and ~5k labeled pairs; 2) Redwood spins up sandbox hosted endpoints and runs evals + a small rerank pipeline; 3) we share benchmark results + cost estimates; 4) if good, kick pilot run with production traffic gated.
[00:09:15] Priya: timeline for that?
[00:09:18] Lena: we'll aim to deliver initial eval in 5 business days after we get the data.
[00:09:22] [00:09:22] Maya: great. a couple of quick follow-ups — do you store training logs? we want to opt out.
[00:09:27] Samir: you can opt out of collection; for hosted we provide that toggle and the audit log shows what was stored. We'll document this in the security pack.
[00:09:39] [00:09:39] [INTERMISSION - quick offline technical question between Samir and Omar about IP allowlists]
[00:14:00] [00:14:00] Omar: if we go hosted, can we restrict by IP and still use SSO?
[00:14:04] Samir: yes, you can use both ip allowlisting and SSO. We'll provide per-API key restrictions in the Console.
[00:14:12] [00:14:12] Samir: i'm going to show the rerank request shape — note we accept candidates as text blobs or ids referencing a stored passage payload, so you can keep PHI out of the direct call by referencing an internal id and letting a private connector resolve it.
[00:14:29] Maya: oh that's good — keeps PHI inside our network.
[00:14:33] Priya: about fallback planning — if hosted capacity is constrained, do you have automated fallback?
[00:14:38] Lena: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible model variant or to a dedicated reserved pool depending on policy. We can set canary percentages and automatic fallback.
[00:14:48] [00:14:48] Samir: also note the separation of control plane vs data plane in Private mode — control in Redwood, data plane in your VPC.
[00:15:00] [00:15:00] Maya: any real-world numbers from similar customers?
[00:15:03] Lena: without naming specifics, customers in health verticals saw a 15-35% improvement in top-1 relevance with a lightweight reranker plus cost reductions when using caching. We'll try to run a similar eval.
[00:15:18] [00:15:18] Priya: ok last product q — do you support structured output from reranker, like JSON with fields?
[00:15:22] Samir: yes, function-calling style outputs and structured annotations are supported; you can ask the reranker to return a justification snippet + category tags.
[00:15:32] [00:15:32] Maya: great. any legal or procurement questions?
[00:15:36] Priya: procurement asks about indemnity and data processing agreement.
[00:15:40] Lena: we'll hand over the DPA and standard terms; enterprise negotiations can adjust clauses. I'll loop in legal in follow-up.
[00:15:49] [00:15:49] Samir: demo: i'll run a slightly larger batch to show batching and cost benefit. (exec) embedding batch 16 -> amortized GPU time lower, throughput up.
[00:16:10] [00:16:10] Samir: Console shows cost estimate drop ~27% with quant + batching, here's the CSV export.
[00:16:20] Maya: can you export the trace to our audit log? we need to keep the demo artifacts.
[00:16:24] Samir: i can export a sanitized trace — will send it with the deck.
[00:16:30] [00:16:30] Priya: from a UX POV we want rerank reasons surfaced to clinicians. is the extractive highlight explainable enough?
[00:16:35] Samir: it's a model explanation, so not provably causal, but useful for triage. We also support deterministic score contributions from lexical features if you want hybrid explainability.
[00:16:50] [00:16:50] Maya: ok, let's talk pilot success metrics — what should we measure?
[00:16:54] Lena: typical metrics: top-1 accuracy lift on labeled set, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), latency p95, cost per query. We'll help instrument and report.
[00:17:06] [00:17:06] Samir: i'll attach a sample telemetry dashboard and a spreadsheet template for metrics.
[00:17:12] [00:17:12] Priya: good. one more — can we enable per-tenant model configs? we have multi-tenant customers with different compliance.
[00:17:18] Lena: yes, you can attach route-level configs and enforce different models or retention rules per tenant.
[00:17:25] [00:17:25] Omar: any blockers with our internal firewall? we typically only allow outbound on a few ports.
[00:17:29] Samir: we only need HTTPS outbound to our API endpoints; on Private we do more advanced tunneling. We'll share the exact CIDR list.
[00:17:40] [00:17:40] [Sidenote: brief audio cut, Samir repeats a line]
[00:20:00] [00:20:00] Samir: ok summarizing the pilot deliverables again: eval w/ labeled pairs, bench runs, config recs (batching/quant), security docs.
[00:20:10] Maya: we'll try to get the sample data by Wednesday.
[00:20:14] Lena: perfect. i'll follow up with an email containing the SOC2 pack, network diagram, and the pricing/sizing grid.
[00:20:22] Priya: can you also share the rerank notebook and the Console link for the sandbox?
[00:20:26] Samir: yes, sending both.
[00:20:29] [00:20:29] [Crosstalk — quick chat about calendar invites]
[00:25:00] [00:25:00] Maya: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[00:25:03] Lena: thanks, we'll send notes and action items.
[00:25:06] Omar: appreciate it.
[00:25:08] Priya: bye.
[00:25:10] [END]
